# qweave v0.6.1

[中文](https://github.com/GaomingOrion/qweave/blob/v0.6.1/.github/release-notes/v0.6.1.md)

This release addresses [issue #1](https://github.com/GaomingOrion/qweave/issues/1)
with common time-series operators and Qlib migration guidance.

## Highlights

- Added Python/Rust `ts_skew`, `ts_kurt`, mean-seeded recursive `ema`, and standard
  linear `wma`, supported by both the tree and DAG engines.
- Skew/Kurt use incremental rolling central moments, with periodic rebuilds and
  additional rebuilds on numerical scale changes to limit accumulated error.
  Full-window, non-finite input, and constant-window rules are preserved.
- `ema(1)` preserves finite inputs exactly, avoiding cancellation when input
  magnitudes change sharply.
- Added bilingual Qlib operator migration tables. On full finite windows,
  `x.wma(20) / qw.lit(20.0)` matches Qlib's extra WMA normalization; warmup and
  missing-value handling still differ.

## Rust WMA Migration

**Breaking Rust API change:** the former Guotai Junan exponential-weighted
`alpha::wma` / `Expr::Wma` are now `alpha::gtja_wma` / `Expr::GtjaWma`.
`alpha::wma` now means standard linear WMA, equivalent to `decay_linear`.
Existing Rust callers needing the Guotai Junan behavior should use `gtja_wma`.
Built-in Alpha191 calls have migrated without changing factor values.

## Installation

```powershell
python -m pip install --upgrade qweave==0.6.1
```

Python 3.10+ is supported through stable-ABI wheels for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
